prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1443; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a report of a minor collision in a parking lot. The claimant, who is not represented by counsel, reported neck pain and was advised to seek medical attention.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone. Their account of the impact was consistent with the initial report, and they described the vehicle as having been stopped when the other car reversed into it.

Entry 3: The police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. The responding officer recorded the location and the position of both cars.

Entry 4: Reviewed the photographs submitted by the claimant. They show damage to the rear bumper and tail light area, which is mostly in line with the impact described. No independent witnesses have come forward.

Entry 5: Confirmed with the insured that the driver involved is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 6: Obtained the vehicle's prior claim and repair history. No earlier damage to the vehicle is recorded, and the repair estimate has been scheduled for review.

Entry 7: The claimant's medical records show initial treatment with a physician, followed by a usual course of physiotherapy. The reported injury fits the kind and force of the collision.

Entry 8: Checked the claimant's history for any prior neck or upper back complaints. None is known, and the claimant has told the same account in every conversation so far.

Entry 9: Follow-up call with the claimant. Symptoms have eased steadily, and the treatment plan is winding down as they recover.

Entry 10: Reviewed the file as a whole. The claim is progressing as expected, with the medical treatment tapering as recovery continues, and the repair estimate is pending final sign-off.
